overview: Uruguay is a small country in south-eastern South America, between Argentina and Brazil. Its capital and largest city is Montevideo, home to about four in ten Uruguayans. Uruguay declared independence in 1825. It hosted and won the first football World Cup, in 1930.

geography.text: Uruguay is mostly low, rolling grassland, used for raising cattle and sheep. It has a long coast on the wide Río de la Plata estuary and the Atlantic Ocean, with beach resorts such as Punta del Este. The Uruguay River forms its border with Argentina.

history.text: Uruguay was fought over by Spain and Portugal, and after independence it became a buffer between Argentina and Brazil; its independence was confirmed in 1828. In the early 1900s it built one of the first welfare states in Latin America. It was ruled by the military from 1973 to 1985.

events.title: Independence confirmed
events.text: A treaty between Argentina and Brazil recognises Uruguay.

events.title: First World Cup
events.text: Uruguay hosts and wins the first football World Cup.

government.text: Uruguay is a presidential republic and one of the most stable democracies in Latin America. The President is elected every five years and cannot serve two terms in a row. Congress has a Chamber of Representatives and a Senate.

economy.text: Uruguay exports beef, soybeans, wood pulp and dairy products. Almost all of its electricity comes from renewable sources, especially wind and hydropower. It has one of the highest incomes per person in Latin America.

culture.text: Uruguay shares tango, mate and asado with Argentina. Candombe, drum music with African roots played in the streets of Montevideo, is listed by UNESCO. Uruguay was one of the first countries to give every school child a laptop, in 2007.

items.title: Candombe
items.text: Afro-Uruguayan drumming parades, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Plan Ceibal
items.text: A laptop for every child, started in 2007.

items.title: Colonia del Sacramento
items.text: A Portuguese colonial town, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Uruguay hosted and won the first ever World Cup in 1930 and won again in 1950, beating hosts Brazil in Rio. It has also won the Copa América 15 times. For a country of about 3.5 million people, its football record is extraordinary.

items.text: The 'Maracanazo': Uruguay beat Brazil in front of 170,000 fans.

items.title: Copa América
items.text: Fifteen titles, second only to Argentina.
